description: Lists the workflow chart templates QuBeSync ships (key, name, description): complete, tested charts for the common multi-step jobs. These match names -- ranked against the connection's name index (ACME, Inc. finds Acme Inc) -- and ask your app about near matches: resolve (any list record by kind and name -- a customer, a job, a vendor, an item, an account -- or the ListID it stored), ensure (resolve, then create what is missing, asking when the name is held elsewhere in its name space), upsert (resolve, then update, or create, asking as ensure does when the name is held elsewhere), push_records (many upserts) and add_transaction (any transaction add, once every customer, item, class or account it names exists: it finds each and asks every question first, then creates what is missing by a rule per kind). The rest: resolve_transaction (a transaction by id, number or GUID); record a payment (asking when it's more than the invoice owes, or the invoice isn't there); void a transaction; read the company's profile (company, preferences, host); pull every record, or those changed and deleted since a date, paged to your app (pull_changes, stream_query). A workflow runs server-side against a connection, settles requests QuickBooks never answered, asks before overwriting a record someone else changed, and can pause for a decision from your app. Workflows run on realtime and simulated connections only (a standard one answers 422 realtime_required). Install one as-is, child workflows included, with POST /api/v2/workflow-templates/{key}/install (body {"publish": true}; add "replace": true to re-install over workflows the app already has); fetch it with get_workflow_template to read or adapt it first.
name: list_workflow_templates
title: List workflow templates
